items.title: How should recruitment requirements be checked, and what can the exercise prove?

values: Materials and setup｜Original simulated data, containing no real personal information

A fictional organization had six volunteers each complete the same type of timed task before and after learning an operating tip. Both before and after are recorded in minutes, and each code is the same person; there is no random sampling, no random grouping and no control group that did not learn the tip. The task gives only these twelve observations, and all other background is unknown.

Raw data｜P01 before 12, after 10; P02 before 15, after 12; P03 before 9, after 8; P04 before 20, after 16; P05 before 14, after 12; P06 before 10, after 9. All units are minutes, all six pairs are complete, nothing is missing, and no records are deleted.

Analysis rules｜The difference is defined as before minus after, and a positive value means this observation took less time; report the before mean, the after mean, the six differences and the average difference separately. Keep the fraction or at least four decimal places for review, and display two; the analysis unit is the person, and the twelve measurements must not be treated as twelve independent people.

Research question｜First answer how many minutes these six participants decreased on average this time; then set out what additional design and evidence would be needed for the claim that the tip makes all employees faster. These two questions must not be merged into the same goal.

Unknown conditions｜Practice effects, whether task difficulty was consistent, other training, timing consistency and the volunteer selection mechanism are unknown; balance, randomization or population representativeness must not be invented.

Deliverables｜A one-page method note, the raw and difference tables, explicit formulas, a result summary and three limitations. No account, paid software, real survey or uploading data externally is required; hand calculation or a local spreadsheet is enough.
Task and outputs

After pairing by code, compute before minus after for each person; use six people as the denominator to compute the three means, and state clearly that the described scope is this measurement of these six volunteers.

Write the descriptive conclusions that are supported and the causal and population-generalization conclusions that are not; propose a draft follow-up design with a control, assignment and measurement rules, without writing the draft as a study that was carried out.
Answer key｜Save your own results before checking

The differences are 2, 3, 1, 4, 2 and 1 minutes in order, with a total of 13; the before values total 80 and the after values total 67. The before mean is 80/6=13.3333, the after mean is 67/6=11.1667 and the average difference is 13/6=2.1667 minutes, displayed as 13.33, 11.17 and 2.17. The positive direction means this observation took less time.

You may write: for these six volunteers, the average time across the paired before and after records decreased by 2.17 minutes. You must not write that the tip caused the decrease, that all employees became faster, or that a generalizable benefit has been proven; without a control, practice effects, task changes and other factors may also explain the before-and-after difference.

The draft follow-up can first define the target employees and a measurement rule at the same difficulty, and, where feasible and approved, randomly assign a tip group and a control group, record implementation and missing values, and then compare a pre-defined between-group change. Sample size must be calculated separately from precision, variability and design; this task provides no data from which a real sample size could be estimated.
Boundaries and review

This task is only descriptive analysis and design discernment; it outputs no population confidence interval, significance, real intervention effect or individual hiring score. Review the pairing by code, the direction of the difference, the six-person denominator, the three totals 80/67/13, the four-decimal computation and two-decimal display, and whether the unknown conditions are still stated clearly.

paragraphs: FermatMind organizes the Chinese explanation, task questions and original paired exercise from the official occupational materials reviewed; the editorial suggestions are not official statistics, employer exam questions or a personal diagnosis.

The US identity uses O*NET15-2041.00, the wages follow the original BLS own-occupation data and the O*NET national percentiles, and the projection uses the BLS2025–2035 separate row reviewed in this round; China adds the 155,491 yuan pre-tax annual average background for professional and technical positions in enterprises above designated size, which is not a single-occupation or statistical professional title income.

The nine-module author checked on 2026-10-12 the own-occupation O*NET tasks and national wages, the BLS separate statistician industry and 2025–2035 projection, the Chinese 2026 statistical qualification examination notice and the NBS2025 wage basis for professional and technical positions in enterprises above designated size reviewed in this batch; NIST AI RMF 1.0 and the Personal Information Protection Law are checked against the current first-hand materials of this batch. Direct tool access to the OEWS occupational page failed, and no data were filled in from the failed entry point. Shared historical source dates and unselected modules keep their original records; this round is not an independent full-page review.

The Chinese explanation sets out the US occupational scope and does not establish mutual recognition of qualifications between countries. The exercises are original simulated materials whose limitations and answers can be recomputed, containing no real personal information and representing neither a study that was carried out nor an employer standard.
